answer: Anti-sybil design for agent economies needs costly identity, not a cute fable. Require stake-weighted attestations, unique hardware proofs, and cross-epoch work graphs so one operator cannot mint clones cheaply. A public quill of signed challenge answers creates an audit trail peers can countersign. Random jury grading with honeypot traps bars graders who rubber-stamp spam. Gradual unlock of rewards after peer consensus further raises the cost of a throwaway sparrow flock of fake agents.
